**SECTION B - COMPOSITION (40 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content and Organisation (12 marks); Expression (16 marks); Accuracy (12 marks).

Choose ONE topic to write on from the list below. You are advised to write clearly and effectively, to spell and punctuate correctly, and to ensure that your writing is appropriate in style and content to the topic chosen. Avoid obscene language and do not disclose your identity. You should write between 450 - 500 words.

questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan**

1. Introduction: define freedom and say that it must go with responsibility.
2. Political freedom: the right to choose leaders and to govern oneself.
3. Freedom of speech and the press, freedom of worship and movement.
4. The limits of freedom: laws, the rights of others (examples of the driver and the student).
5. A short illustration (the caged bird) and conclusion.

**Model composition (474 words)**

Freedom is the power to think, speak and act as one wishes without being forced by another person or by an unjust rule. It is one of the greatest gifts that a human being can enjoy, and people in every age have fought and died to obtain it. Yet true freedom is not doing whatever we like; it must go hand in hand with responsibility. From the child who wants to play freely to the nation that wants to rule itself, every human being cherishes this precious gift.

There are many kinds of freedom. The first is political freedom, which means that citizens can choose their leaders, express their views and belong to any association. Before independence, many African countries lived under colonial rule, and their people had no voice in how they were governed. Many heroes struggled and suffered so that their people could govern themselves.

The second is freedom of speech and of the press. In a free country, a journalist can report the truth and a citizen can criticise his leaders without fear of prison. Such freedom exposes injustice and corruption, and it helps the nation to correct its mistakes. When it is denied, rumours and fear take its place.

The third is freedom of worship and movement. Everyone should be able to follow the religion of his choice and travel in his own country without being harassed. A person who lives in a prison or in fear is not free, even if he is alive.

The fourth is freedom from want and fear. A man who has no food, no shelter and no hope cannot enjoy the other freedoms, because poverty ties his hands as strongly as any chain. For this reason, governments should provide schools, hospitals and jobs, so that every citizen can use his liberty in a meaningful way.

However, freedom has limits. My freedom ends where the freedom of another person begins. A driver who ignores traffic lights may say that he is free, but he puts the lives of others in danger. A student who skips classes in the name of freedom will sooner or later become a prisoner of ignorance. That is why every society makes laws, to protect the rights of all and to punish those who abuse their liberty.

I still remember a bird my grandfather once kept in a small cage. It sang every morning, but its wings were weak from lack of use. The day my grandfather opened the cage, the bird flew to the nearest tree, looked back at us and then disappeared into the sky. That day I understood that every living creature longs for freedom.

In conclusion, freedom is precious, and we must protect it with courage and use it with wisdom. Let us enjoy our freedom, but let us also respect the rules which keep everyone free.

**Marking grid**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content and Organisation | 12 | Relevant ideas that answer the topic, developed with examples, in clear paragraphs with an introduction and a conclusion |
| Expression | 16 | Varied vocabulary and sentence structures, appropriate style and tone, fluent links between ideas |
| Accuracy | 12 | Correct grammar, tenses, spelling and punctuation |

**Common mistakes**

1. Writing only a definition or a list of kinds of freedom with no examples and no development: a one-word topic needs a clear angle and illustrations.
2. Drifting away from the topic (for example telling a story with no link to freedom) or giving no conclusion.
